source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's San Antonio campus publishes 36 MW of IT capacity, the fourth-largest disclosed figure in Texas, where only 19 of 133 mapped data centers report capacity at all.

The campus covers 295,785 square feet of technical space across three buildings, SAT2 through SAT4. Its certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, SSAE 16 Type II and TIA-942, describe a facility built for regulated enterprise and cloud tenants. That tenant profile is not the same as a purpose-built accelerator training cluster. The 36 MW equals 7.6 percent of the 475 MW Texas discloses across its 19 reporting facilities.

For AI, the binding number is power, and the published data stops at IT capacity. No grid connection capacity, backup generation, or delivery limit is disclosed. Whether 36 MW is a campus power ceiling or an equipment limit is therefore unknown. At 40 kW per rack the capacity implies roughly 900 racks, but the operator publishes no tenant mix and no utilization, so real accelerator density cannot be derived from it.

What the data does not cover is most of Texas. Only 19 of 133 mapped locations publish capacity, so the state's actual total and any AI-driven pressure on it stay invisible. The suitability score of 68 rests on published IT capacity and operator type alone, with announced expansion listed as missing. Texas ranks second nationally in published data center capacity, so the undisclosed remainder is large relative to what is counted.
